request: How large is the immigration court backlog and how has it changed over time?

reply.reply:
**At the end of FY2024, the immigration court backlog stood at 3,558,995 pending cases; caseloads have generally risen since 1983, with annual receipts increasing more significantly since FY2019.**

- At the end of FY2024, EOIR had 3,558,995 pending cases. (IN12492, PDF p. 4)
- Immigration court caseloads have generally increased since EOIR was established in 1983, with annual receipts rising more significantly since FY2019 except in FY2020 and FY2021. (IN12492, PDF p. 2)
- In FY2024, immigration judges completed 701,749 cases, while EOIR received an average of 148,663 new cases per month. (IN12492, PDF p. 4)
reply.reasoning: The latest CRS data located directly states the FY2024 pending-case total and describes long-run caseload growth. It also shows that completions lagged far behind receipts during FY2024.
